description_record.title: Trump sons-backed Powerus merger closes; Aureus adopts the Powerus name
description_record.description_short: Trump sons-backed Powerus merger closes; Aureus adopts Powerus Corporation name
description_record.description_medium: Powerus and Aureus Greenway Holdings announced on October 1, 2026, that their previously announced merger had closed. Legacy Powerus survived the combination, Aureus adopted the Powerus Corporation name, and the public company continued trading on Nasdaq as PUSA. Breaking Defense reported that the Trump brothers backed Aureus through their stake in American Ventures.
description_record.description_long: On October 1, 2026, Powerus and Aureus Greenway Holdings announced that their previously announced merger had closed. Powerus survived the combination; Aureus changed its name to Powerus Corporation, and the combined public company continued trading on Nasdaq as PUSA. The SEC filing dates the reported event October 1 and describes the merger closing. Breaking Defense identified Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump as backers of Aureus through their stake in American Ventures. The transaction had been planned months earlier, so this record concerns the October 1 closing rather than the announcement of a proposed merger. The company release describes Powerus merging into a newly formed Aureus subsidiary, while the SEC filing supplies the formal closing record. The available sources establish a family-linked investment connection but do not establish that the brothers directed the transaction, secured government business through it, or engaged in misconduct. They also do not establish that the sons held direct Powerus shares.

review_reasons: Dated event and family/private-interest connection are source-supported; candidate remains proposed pending editorial review.

description_record.title: Powerus PUSA shares begin trading as a token on Solana through Backpack and Sunrise
description_record.description_short: Powerus PUSA token launches on Solana through Backpack Securities and Sunrise
description_record.description_medium: On October 2, Sunrise announced that PUSA was listed on Solana through its platform, with issuance by Backpack Securities. Backpack said the token was redeemable one-for-one for Powerus Corporation shares and transferable to traditional brokerages. This followed the October 1 merger and is a separate market-access launch, not another report of the merger closing.
description_record.description_long: On October 2, 2026, Sunrise announced that PUSA was listed on Solana, with Backpack Securities as issuer. Backpack said each token could be redeemed one-for-one for Powerus Corporation shares and transferred to traditional brokerages. The official posts identify the token contract address, while contemporaneous Solana Compass reporting places the listing at 14:56 UTC. Sunrise and Backpack published the same mint address and told users to verify it before trading. The listing came one day after the merger that made Powerus Corporation a Nasdaq-traded company. It is a distinct distribution and trading event, not a second description of the merger. Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump were reported to have an indirect stake in the company through American Ventures; the sources do not establish that either son directed or participated in the token listing, and the token representation should not be confused with a new issuance of Powerus common stock.

review_reasons: Dated event and family/private-interest connection are source-supported; candidate remains proposed pending editorial review.

description_record.title: Trump-family-linked WLFI signs USD1 cooperation MOU with MOA Protocol in Seoul
description_record.description_short: Trump-linked WLFI and MOA Protocol sign exploratory USD1 finance MOU in Seoul
description_record.description_medium: At a joint event in Seoul on October 1, 2026, World Liberty Financial and MOA Protocol signed a memorandum of understanding on possible USD1 use in financial services and payments. The signing was attributed to MOA CEO Stefan Piech and WLFI business chief Ryan Ballantyne. Coverage said no service launch date or completed integration was disclosed. Reuters identifies Donald Trump and his sons as WLFI co-founders.
description_record.description_long: The two companies signed an MOU at their October 1 “My Own Access” event at Grand Hyatt Seoul during Korea Blockchain Week. MOA Protocol CEO Stefan Piech and WLFI chief business officer Ryan Ballantyne signed. Coverage described possible uses of USD1 in yield management, treasury, payments, commerce and cross-border services. Reuters has reported that Donald Trump and his sons are co-founders of WLFI, placing the agreement within the family-linked venture lane. The sources describe an exploratory cooperation framework: they do not disclose detailed contractual terms, a launch timetable, a completed integration or actual transaction volumes. Blockchain Seoul notes that the public event materials did not specify the implementation schedule or confirm that any proposed connection was live. The public reporting also does not reproduce the full MOU text. This record is the signing itself, not a claim that planned services were deployed or that the partnership produced revenue.

review_reasons: Dated event and family/private-interest connection are source-supported; candidate remains proposed pending editorial review.

description_record.title: WLFI launches staking and seeds a $1.25 million USD1 rewards pool
description_record.description_short: WLFI activates staking and funds its initial $1.25M USD1 rewards pool
description_record.description_medium: World Liberty Financial said WLFI staking was live on October 1, after a community vote. The company reported that it seeded the initial $1.25 million USD1 pool on October 2. It said users must lock unlocked WLFI for at least 180 days and vote at least once every 90 days; rewards are variable and not guaranteed.
description_record.description_long: WLFI’s official account announced on October 1 that its staking program was live after a community vote and that a $1.25 million USD1 reward pool would be funded the next day. On October 2, the account said the pool had been seeded and that further deposits would occur every two weeks. The company described eligibility conditions requiring at least a 180-day lock of unlocked WLFI and a governance vote at least once every 90 days. It also cautioned that rates could change and that rewards were not guaranteed. Reuters identifies Donald Trump and his sons as WLFI co-founders. The dated event is the program launch and initial funding; these company posts do not independently verify future payouts or a guaranteed yield. A September 14 governance forum proposal had recommended the program launch by October 1, but the October 1 company post is the evidence that it actually went live.

review_reasons: Dated event and family/private-interest connection are source-supported; candidate remains proposed pending editorial review.

description_record.title: Kushner calls CNN’s Israel-investment report misleading and disputes its conflict implication
description_record.description_short: Kushner rebuts CNN report on Affinity’s Phoenix investment and military-linked firms
description_record.description_medium: On October 2, Jared Kushner posted that CNN’s prior-day report was misleading and rejected the suggestion that his Middle East diplomacy benefited Israeli defense-company investments. He said Affinity Partners’ investment in Phoenix predated Trump’s reelection, that Phoenix was a financial institution rather than a defense company, and that Affinity did not own the firms highlighted. These are Kushner’s claims, not independent findings.
description_record.description_long: Jared Kushner responded on October 2 to CNN’s October 1 investigation of Affinity Partners’ investment in Phoenix Financial and Phoenix’s holdings in companies supplying Israel’s military. In a post on X, he called the report and headline “deeply misleading,” said the Phoenix investment predated President Trump’s reelection and his return to public service, and argued that Affinity did not own the defense companies CNN discussed. He also said he had no role in Phoenix’s investment decisions. The Hill reported the post the same day. CNN’s investigation cited Israeli financial records and reported that Affinity was Phoenix’s largest shareholder, while describing Phoenix—not Affinity—as the direct holder of the investments it reviewed. CNN said it found no indication that Kushner’s diplomatic actions directly affected the investments; the competing statements do not resolve the broader ethics question. This record covers Kushner’s dated response, not the earlier investment or CNN’s separate publication.

review_reasons: Dated event and family/private-interest connection are source-supported; candidate remains proposed pending editorial review.
